To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the IoT is complex and the complexity is increasing, that IoT systems are becoming more and more distributed, that IoT systems require an ontology that includes semantics, that IoT ontologies must be able to support the full understanding of system flow, services, and quality, and that a focus on IoT FSQ semantics is necessary.
IoT systems require a full understanding of the FSQ of the IoT architecture.
a semantic IoT ontology must be extended to include a full understanding of FSQ in order to be useful to IoT designers, operators, users, and other stakeholders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of semantic ontologies in IoT applications and how these semantic ontologies can be extended to include FSQ definitions.
the definition of a semantic ontology to describe the IoT environment, the system architecture, and the FSQ semantics in IoT systems.
how the semantic IoT ontology is used to support the design, implementation, and operation of IoT systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a semantic IoT ontology is a key component for the successful design, development and implementation of IoT systems.
IoT semantic ontologies must be expanded to include a full understanding of the FSQ of the system and its entities.
IoT systems must be understood at all levels, from the hardware to the services and qualities of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current state of semantic IoT ontology does not support the full range of IoT systems, but it could be extended with the inclusion of FSQ semantics and the use of a formal ontology language.
a semantic ontology for an IoT system should include a description of the IoT system, the entities in the IoT system, and the FSQ semantics in the IoT system.
the current use of ontologies in IoT systems is insufficient for the needs of the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the current use of sematic ontologies in IoT systems does not include a full understanding of FSQ in IoT applications and that this understanding is necessary for IoT system designers, operators, users, and developers.
a semantic ontology for IoT systems should include the semantics of the IoT architecture, system flows, services and qualities, and the entities in an IoT system.

the IoT community should be able to leverage the power of semantic ontologies for IoT systems to improve the understanding and operation of the IoT systems and to improve the quality of the data produced.
